title: AI-Assisted Discovery of CNOT Decompositions for Quantum Permutations on Constrained Topologies
abstract: arXiv:2610.37045v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efficient quantum circuit compilation is challenging for quantum computers, where limited qubit connectivity can introduce substantial overhead in the implementation of logical operations. Recent AI-assisted synthesis methods have shown considerable potential for reducing circuit complexity, but their role in uncovering principles that can guide the design of new deterministic compilation algorithms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate this perspective for the synthesis of quantum permutations into CNOT circuits under constrained qubit connectivity. Using AlphaCNOT as an exploratory tool, we identify a recurring decomposition for remote transpositions that improves on the construction based on adjacent SWAP routing. For two qubits at graph distance $d>1$, the discovered pattern yields a topology-legal implementation using at most $6d-4$ CNOT gates, compared to the $6d-3$ gates required by the corresponding SWAP-based

translated_title: AI辅助发现受限拓扑上量子置换的CNOT分解
translated_abstract: 高效的量子线路编译对量子计算机而言是一项挑战，因为受限的量子比特连接性会给逻辑运算的实现带来显著的开销。近期AI辅助的合成方法在降低线路复杂度方面已展现出相当大的潜力，但它们在揭示能够指导新型确定性编译算法设计的原理方面的作用在很大程度上仍未被探索。在这项工作中，我们针对受限量子比特连接条件下量子置换到CNOT线路的合成问题，从这一视角展开研究。利用AlphaCNOT作为探索工具，我们发现了一种针对远程对换的可复用分解模式，改进了基于相邻SWAP路由的构造方法。对于图距离为 $d>1$ 的两个量子比特，所发现的模式给出了一种拓扑合法的实现方案，最多使用 $6d-4$ 个CNOT门，而相应的基于SWAP的方法则需要 $6d-3$ 个门。
tldr: 本研究利用AI工具AlphaCNOT探索发现了一种受限拓扑下远程对换的CNOT分解模式，使图距离为d的两个量子比特间的置换最多仅需6d-4个CNOT门，优于基于SWAP路由的6d-3个门的构造，展示了AI在揭示新型确定性编译算法设计原理方面的价值。
en_tdlr: Using AlphaCNOT as an exploratory AI tool, this work discovers a recurring decomposition for remote transpositions on constrained qubit topologies, achieving topology-legal implementations with at most 6d-4 CNOT gates for qubits at graph distance d, improving upon the 6d-3 gates required by SWAP-based constructions and demonstrating AI's role in uncovering principles for new deterministic compilation algorithms.
